subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable API boundary affects shared media code, bundled plugins, and plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that product/API direction by itself.

options.title: Use media-core or plugin-safe SDK boundary
options.body: Move the decoder into a shared boundary that channel plugins can consume, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that one helper.

options.title: Keep narrow channel repairs for now
options.body: Treat existing Feishu fixes as sufficient until concrete non-Feishu encoding failures are reported.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep the issue open but ask for live or source-level non-Feishu failures before approving a shared multi-encoding utility.

recommendation.title: Use media-core or plugin-safe SDK boundary
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into a shared boundary that channel plugins can consume, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that one helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Feishu filename merge and adjacent media-core history make this the best available owner for the boundary choice.
